title: Essentially of finite presentation over an intermediate algebra essentially of finite type
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ and $\psi:S\to S'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Assume that $S$ is essentially of finite type over $R$ via $\varphi$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], and that $S'$ is essentially of finite presentation over $R$ via $\psi\circ\varphi$: $S'$ is isomorphic, as an $R$-algebra, to a localization $W^{-1}P$ of a finitely presented $R$-algebra $P$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq P$. Then $S'$ is essentially of finite presentation over $S$ via $\psi$: there are a finitely presented $S$-algebra $P'$ and a multiplicative subset $V\subseteq P'$ such that $S'\cong V^{-1}P'$ as $S$-algebras.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), first paragraph, where it is used without statement ('there exist $g_{j,\lambda_2}$ ... such that $S'=\colim S'_\lambda$, with $S'_\lambda=(S_\lambda[y_1,\dots,y_m]/(\bar g_{1,\lambda},\dots,\bar g_{v,\lambda}))_{\bar{\mathfrak q}'_\lambda}$', which presents $S'$ as a localization of a finitely presented $S$-algebra); it is the analogue, for 'essentially of finite type/presentation' (definition-essentially-finite-p-t, line 12836), of Lemma Tag 00F4 (4) (lemma-compose-finite-type, line 540). Stacks states no such lemma.

proof.text: Choose presentations $S\cong W^{-1}B$ as $R$-algebras, with $B$ generated over $R$ by $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $S'\cong U^{-1}P$ as $R$-algebras, with $P$ finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Transport $\psi$ through these isomorphisms. The image of $b_i/1$ in $U^{-1}P$ has a representative $p_i/u_i$ with $p_i\in P$, $u_i\in U$, for each $i$. These are finitely many choices even though $W$ and $U$ need not be finitely generated.

source.place: Definition 00QM (definition-essentially-finite-p-t), Definition 00F3 (definition-finite-type), and Proposition 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization); the finite choices are made by an agent

proof.text: Set $A=S\otimes_RP$, viewed as an $S$-algebra, and let $Q=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(u_it_i-1,\ b_i\otimes1-1\otimes p_i\,t_i\mid 1\le i\le n)$, where $u_i$ and $p_i$ denote $1\otimes u_i$ and $1\otimes p_i$ in $A$. The $S$-algebra $A$ is finitely presented by base change from $P$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Adjoining finitely many polynomial variables is of finite presentation by the definition [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; quotienting by the displayed finite set of relations preserves finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal]. Hence $Q$ is a finitely presented $S$-algebra, by composition [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition].

source.place: Lemma 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), item (4); Lemma 00F4 (lemma-compose-finite-type), proof of item (4), where finitely many equations for the images of generators are imposed; the localized construction is by an agent

proof.text: The $S$-algebra maps $S\xrightarrow{\psi}U^{-1}P$ and $P\to U^{-1}P$ give an $S$-algebra map $A\to U^{-1}P$. Send $t_i$ to $1/u_i$. The relation $u_it_i=1$ holds, and $b_i\otimes1-1\otimes p_i\,t_i$ maps to $\psi(b_i/1)-p_i/u_i=0$, so this induces an $S$-algebra map $Q\to U^{-1}P$. It sends the image of each $u\in U$ to a unit, and thus extends uniquely to $\theta:V^{-1}Q\to U^{-1}P$, where $V$ is the image of $U$ in $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] (the localization universal property).

source.place: Proposition 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), existence and uniqueness; the map and relation checks are by an agent

proof.text: The localization map $P\to V^{-1}Q$ sends $U$ to units, hence gives an $R$-algebra map $\eta:U^{-1}P\to V^{-1}Q$ by Proposition 00CP. The composite $\theta\eta$ fixes $P$ and therefore fixes all $p/u\in U^{-1}P$. Conversely, $\eta\theta$ fixes $1\otimes P$ and $t_i$ (since $t_i=u_i^{-1}$ in $Q$). It fixes $b_i\otimes1$ because the second defining relation says $b_i\otimes1=p_it_i=\eta(\psi(b_i/1))$. Since $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B$ over $R$, it fixes the image of $B$ in $S\otimes_RP$; since the images of all $w\in W$ are units in $S$, it also fixes their inverses and hence the image of all of $S=W^{-1}B$. Thus it fixes $A$, then $Q$, then the inverses of $V$, so $\eta\theta=\mathrm{id}$. Therefore $S'\cong U^{-1}P\cong V^{-1}Q$ as $S$-algebras, with $Q$ finitely presented over $S$ by step 2.

lean.statement: theorem essentially_finite_presentation_over_intermediate {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {T : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T] (φ : R →+* S) (ψ : S →+* T) (hS : φ.EssFiniteType) (P : Type p) [CommRing P] [Algebra R P] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R P] (U : Submonoid P) (f : P →+* T) (hf : f.comp (algebraMap R P) = ψ.comp φ) (hT : letI := f.toAlgebra; IsLocalization U T) : ∃ (Q : Type (max v p)) (_ : CommRing Q) (_ : Algebra S Q), Algebra.FinitePresentation S Q ∧ ∃ (V : Submonoid Q) (g : Q →+* T), g.comp (algebraMap S Q) = ψ ∧ (letI := g.toAlgebra; IsLocalization V T)
